decisions.quote:
Following the conventions of Rabbitt (1968), our next
analysis was conducted only on the first half of the list, and demonstrated that the
presence of noise in the second half significantly impaired recall of the first half, F(1,
199) = 22.4, p < 0.001. This result replicates the key finding reported in Rabbitt (1968)—
indeed, the magnitude of the effect of noise in the second half of the list on recall of the
first half of the list in our study was identical to that in Rabbitt’s original experiment
(Cohen’s d = 0.19 for both; see Figure 2).
decisions.reason: Guang et al. (2021) conducted a direct replication of Rabbitt (1968) Experiment 2 in a new online sample (record_type = replication, resolved target = Rabbitt, 1968). Across the original absolute-scoring ANOVA, partial-scoring ANOVA, and generalized linear mixed-effects models, the authors explicitly conclude that they replicated Rabbitt's main finding that subsequent masking noise in the second half of a digit list impairs recall of items from the first half, with an identical effect size (Cohen's d = 0.19). The non-significant interaction between first-half and second-half noise is explicitly identified by the authors as a novel extension not tested in Rabbitt (1968). Therefore, both the shipped coding and blind coding are correct that the replication outcome is 'successful'.
